subject: Service accountability & proposed credit construct
messages:
From: Emmett Clarke <emmett.clarke@aurorahealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@aurorahealth.ai
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe degradation this morning — request for exec bridge and credit discussion

Karthik,

We experienced sustained latency spikes and a high 5xx rate across our busiest inference endpoints between 03:40–05:20 PDT this morning. Throughput dropped by ~40% and several production workflows degraded. Our SREs attached sample logs and trace IDs. This impacted several patient-facing features in the mobile app during peak hours.

We need two things quickly:
- An exec bridge to understand root cause and immediate mitigations (we are available now through 18:00 PT).
- A preliminary statement on commercial remediation — our procurement team will want an estimate of credits and a timeline for the final calculation.

Please escalate. We are blocking on this for an urgent customer call on Monday.

Best,
Emmett Clarke
CTO, Aurora Health

Attachments: aurora-error-sample-logs.txt (txt, 78KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Emmett Clarke <emmett.clarke@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe degradation this morning — request for exec bridge and credit discussion

Emmett — thank you for the heads up and for the logs. We’re very sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in our on-call infra lead (Jonas) and commercial/legal (Marissa) so we can:

1) Stand up an exec bridge in the next 30 minutes to walk through the impact and runbook. Suggested bridge time: 17:15 PT. Confirm if that works.
2) Provide an initial credit construct by EOD tomorrow and a detailed calculation within 72 hours, once our telemetry team finalizes the incident window.

Jonas — can you please start a quick triage and share a short incident snapshot on the call?
Marissa — heads up on the commercial ask; we’ll need the contract references (SLA section + credit formula) and a proposed customer-facing note.

I’ll start the bridge invitation and share notes; tagging Dev for logs correlation.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, Emmett Clarke <emmett.clarke@aurorahealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe degradation this morning — request for exec bridge and credit discussion

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 5:05 PM PDT Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jonas — can you please start a quick triage and share a short incident snapshot on the call?

Quick triage notes for the bridge:
- Symptom: elevated tail latency (p95/p99) and spike in 502/504 responses across two inference pools serving aurora-prod (region: us-west-2).
- Time window affecting customer: 03:40–05:20 PDT (matches Aurora logs).
- Root cause (early): autoscaler mis-evaluation + one faulty GPU node that tripped health checks; combined with aggressive request burst produced KV-cache thrashing in the older q4f quantized variants.
- Mitigation applied: drained the faulty node, widened autoscaler threshold, forced traffic to stable model variant; p99 returned to baseline by 05:40 PDT.
- Impact estimate: roughly 38–45% throughput reduction for 100 minutes; error rate spike to 6.2% in the window.

I’ll share a short incident snapshot deck on the drive and will stay on the bridge for the first 30 minutes.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-snapshot.md (uploaded to drive)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, Emmett Clarke <emmett.clarke@aurorahealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe degradation this morning — request for exec bridge and credit discussion

Thanks — summary and commercial posture below.

Legal/Commercial context (short): the Aurora Health MSA refers to the Service Level section (Section 4) and the "Service Credits" clause. The contract's credit formula ties credits to the percent of downtime/ degraded throughput during the measured window. We should move quickly but need to:
- Confirm precise incident window and per-tenant metrics (Jonas to confirm).
- Provide a transparent credit calc that reconciles to their usage billing for the month.
- Offer a limited goodwill add-on (e.g., token uplift or 1-month discount) to preserve the relationship — propose this only with approval from revenue ops.

Proposed customer-facing language (draft):
"Redwood apologizes for the disruption on May 1, 2027. We have identified a root cause and applied mitigations. Per the contract, we propose a provisional credit of X% of the monthly invoice proportionate to measured degraded throughput during 03:40–05:20 PDT; a final calculation will be delivered within 72 hours after telemetry reconciliation. Additionally, as a gesture of goodwill, Redwood will provide a token uplift of 100k generation tokens (valid for 90 days)."

I attached a proposed-credit-worksheet.csv with a placeholder calculation. Dev/Finance: please review the numbers and estimated impact; we need an initial figure before we send the external note.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Emmett Clarke <emmett.clarke@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe degradation this morning — request for exec bridge and credit discussion

Emmett — thank you again for joining the bridge on Saturday. Follow-up and next steps: 

1) Incident recap: our initial telemetry shows a 100-minute degradation window from 03:40–05:20 PDT on May 1. Root cause: combined autoscaler mis-evaluation + single-node health failure causing cache pressure on q4f variants; we have deployed a safeguard to prevent recurrence. Jonas will send the final telemetry snapshot by EOD today.

2) Provisional commercial offer (subject to final telemetry reconciliation):
- Provisional credit: 15% of Aurora’s May monthly usage bill, prorated to the affected endpoints during the incident window (see attached worksheet).
- Goodwill: one-time grant of 100k generation tokens, valid for 90 days.
- Timeline: Final credit calculation and formal credit note by Thursday, May 6 (72 hours after telemetry reconciliation).

3) Ask of Aurora: please confirm receipt and that the proposed timelines work for your procurement/legal teams. If you need a formal amendment or a one-off invoice adjustment we’ll coordinate with Marissa and our revenue ops.

Attached: proposed-credit-worksheet.csv; exec-bridge-notes.docx

Thanks — we want to make this right.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Emmett Clarke <emmett.clarke@aurorahealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@aurorahealth.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Karthik — appreciate the quick response and the provisional offer. Procurement wants a short executive call with Redwood leadership this week to review the final remediation and the credit math before sign-off. Can you confirm availability for Wednesday (May 5) between 09:00–12:00 PT?

Also, please ensure the final calculation includes: per-endpoint token counts, the exact degraded request volumes, and any compensatory tokens already consumed. We will need a formal credit note and an updated invoice-line for accounting.

Emmett
CTO, Aurora Health
